title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow?

items.stem: Which statement correctly separates a workflow from an agent?

options.text: A workflow never calls a model, while an agent always does
A workflow uses tools, while an agent only writes plain text
A workflow follows steps the code fixes, while an agent picks its own
A workflow answers once, while an agent must always run longer

items.stem: Every booking request at the makerspace needs the same three steps in the same order: check the calendar, book the slot if it is free, then email the student a confirmation. Which design fits best?

options.text: A fixed workflow, because the order is known before the request arrives
An agent, because booking needs a tool and tools require an agent
An agent, because the model can then choose any order it likes
A fixed workflow, because workflows never need to call the model

items.stem: In one sentence: in the makerspace assistant, who decides which tool is called next in an agent, and who decides it in a workflow?

A student writes: "My 3D print keeps peeling off the bed and I don't know why." The right steps depend on what the manuals say and what the student answers, and nobody can list them in advance. Which design fits this request best?

options.text: A fixed workflow with one hard-coded step for every possible cause
A fixed workflow, because it always costs less than any agent
A fixed workflow, because the manuals are the same every time
An agent, because the number and order of steps cannot be known

items.stem: Assume every model call costs $0.02. A fixed workflow answers a manual question with exactly 2 model calls. An agent answering the same question makes 1 call per tool request plus 1 for the final answer, and on average it makes 4 tool requests. How many more dollars does the agent cost than the workflow over 100 such questions?

The assistant's code first asks a model to label each question "manual" or "booking". The code then runs one fixed sequence of steps for "manual" and a different fixed sequence for "booking". Is this a workflow or an agent?

options.text: An agent, because a model's output decides which path runs
A workflow, because the code owns the paths and the model only picks one
An agent, because it uses more than one model call per request
A workflow, because a model never influences which steps run
